domain: environmental regulation / permit compliance breach prediction
prediction_question: Would a permitted waste/installation site incur at least one recorded permit condition breach in a given year, from permit/site features? (Lead closed at licence triage before the task was fully framed, per the cheapest-first rule.)
prediction_time: Would have been start of the assessment year (site features + prior breach history); never fully framed because the licence veto came first.
target_definition: Would have been a derived binary from EA Compliance Classification Scheme breach records; the dataset itself carries the licence veto below.

sources.name: Compliance Classification Scheme (condition breaches on EPR waste and installation permits)
sources.api: Yearly ZIP downloads 2014-2024 listed on the dataset page (not fetched past the licence page: the veto is cheaper than the probe)
sources.license: Environment Agency Conditional Licence (NOT OGL) - see licence_note
sources.access: anonymous downloads; access was never the blocker

license_evidence: Read 2026-10-31 from https://environment.data.gov.uk/dataset/5f2149c0-d465-11e4-b632-f0def148f590, Licence section: 'Environment Agency Conditional Licence'; Attribution: 'Environment Agency copyright and/or database right 2025. All rights reserved.'

Use constraints quoted verbatim (same page, read 2026-10-31): '1. You may use the Information for your internal or personal purposes and may only sublicense others to use it if you do so under a written licence which includes the terms of these conditions... 2. The period of permitted use is one year. 3. We have restricted use of the Information as a result of legal restrictions placed upon us to protect the rights or confidentialities of others.'

Use limitation statement (same page): 'There are no public access constraints to this data. Use of this data is subject to the licence identified.' - open ACCESS, closed REDISTRIBUTION; the distinction is exactly the one the discovery triage exists to catch.
rejection_reason: DROPPED at licence triage (cheapest veto, before any volume/schema probe): the EA Conditional Licence permits internal/personal use only, for a one-year term, with sublicensing only under a written EA licence - derived rows cannot be published. The task idea (predict next-year permit breach from site features + history; the US EPA's published RCRA violation-forecasting model shows the regulatory utility pattern) stays unprobed and unclaimed. What would reopen it: EA relicensing this dataset (or its successor compliance products) under OGL, or a candidate-specific operator decision to seek written permission - a class C enquiry we do not send unsolicited under the standing policy.
next_action: None. Closed; reopen only on new licence evidence per rejection_reason.
licence_note: Class D on the publisher's own instrument. The dataset page (Defra Data Services Platform, read 2026-10-31) names the licence as the 'Environment Agency Conditional Licence' with attribution 'Environment Agency copyright and/or database right... All rights reserved' and special conditions that permit only internal/personal use, cap permitted use at one year, and allow sublicensing only 'under a written licence' from the Agency. That does not permit redistributing derived rows as a public dataset. SCOPE: this veto is for this dataset/instrument only - it does NOT generalize to the Environment Agency's other products, many of which (bathing waters, flood warnings, river levels) are published under OGL; each EA dataset must be triaged on its own page.
